name: when the saved-accounts list cannot be rewritten the switch is handed over and the snapshot is not marked stale

steps.title: Close Battle.net
steps.detail: Skipped: Battle.net.exe is not running.

steps.title: Save the outgoing session
steps.detail: The UnifiedAuth value holds Main's session; store it, encrypted, as the account's snapshot if it changed. Nothing of the client's changes.

steps.title: Back up Battle.net.config and the UnifiedAuth value
steps.detail: Copy {tmp}\Roaming\Battle.net\Battle.net.config into a new snapshot folder and record 1 UnifiedAuth value in it, vault-encrypted, so a failed switch can be rolled back. The newest 20 snapshots are kept.

steps.title: Put the account's session token in place
steps.detail: Decrypt Alt's session snapshot from the vault and write it as the REG_BINARY value under UnifiedAuth (reg add /t REG_BINARY). Any other value there (the outgoing token, saved in the step above when it belongs to a One Launch account) is removed, the way the client's own logout removes it. The bytes are a DPAPI blob bound to this Windows user and are never shown or logged. Identity, EncryptionKey, Launch Options, and every file under the client's folders stay untouched.

steps.title: Put the login first in the saved-accounts list
steps.detail: Skipped: {tmp}\Roaming\Battle.net\Battle.net.config does not round-trip through One Launch's JSON writer byte for byte, so it is left alone rather than rewritten with a different layout.

steps.title: Start Battle.net
steps.detail: Start Battle.net Launcher.exe with no arguments, as the Start Menu shortcut does (it applies any pending update, then starts the client with --from-launcher). The client signs in as saved3@example.com on its own from the UnifiedAuth token.

steps.title: Wait for the client to come up
steps.detail: Poll the process list until Battle.net.exe is running, up to 0.5 s.

steps.title: Confirm the client signed in
steps.detail: Read the new run's log (battle.net-<timestamp>.log; no tokens in it) until "Logged into Battle.net successfully" names the account id …3d4e, up to 0.5 s. A "Login failed" line means the token was rejected: the snapshot is marked stale and the next step hands over to you.

steps.title: Wait for you to sign in
steps.detail: Runs only if the client rejects the stored token or does not sign in within 0.5 s. The client stays on its login page; you sign in there once as saved3@example.com with "Keep me logged in" on, and One Launch continues with the game as soon as the log reports the sign-in, up to 0.016666666666666666 min.

steps.title: Save the new session
steps.detail: Runs only after a manual sign-in: the fresh UnifiedAuth value replaces the stale snapshot.

warnings: {tmp}\Roaming\Battle.net\Battle.net.config has a layout One Launch cannot reproduce exactly, so the saved-accounts step is skipped rather than rewriting the file differently.
saved3@example.com cannot be put first in Client.SavedAccountNames (see the saved-accounts step), and the client only accepts the token of the login that is first, so it will ask for the password.

steps.title: Close Battle.net
steps.detail: Skipped: Battle.net.exe is not running.

steps.title: Save the outgoing session
steps.detail: Main's stored session is already current.

steps.title: Back up Battle.net.config and the UnifiedAuth value
steps.detail: {tmp}\backups\battlenet\<ts>

steps.detail: UnifiedAuth now holds the snapshot (fingerprint 59028191).
